claim: Let \(X\) be the four corners of a Euclidean square of side \(2\), and let \(Y\) be obtained by adjoining its center. For the isometric inclusion \(X\hookrightarrow Y\), the induced map \(\mathrm{MH}_{2,4\sqrt2}(X;\mathbb Z)\to\mathrm{MH}_{2,4\sqrt2}(Y;\mathbb Z)\) is zero, with source \(\mathbb Z^4\) and target \(0\).
integrity: Exact symbolic distance arithmetic and an exhaustive finite chain enumeration support the explicit proof. Independent external validation has not been performed.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns only the bidegree (2, 4*sqrt(2)) for the specified five-point Euclidean metric space and its four-point subspace.
No general injectivity theorem for magnitude homology is claimed.
title: A five-point isometric extension kills square-loop magnitude homology
